title: Minimal Change Disease: Pathophysiology, Signs and Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Minimal change disease
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Foot process effacement is the characteristic electron-microscopic finding.
Light microscopy may show little or no obvious abnormality.
Nephrotic syndrome is a typical presentation, especially in children.
Corticosteroid responsiveness is common, although relapse may occur.

title: Nephrotic Syndrome: Pathophysiology, Signs and Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Nephrotic syndrome
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Heavy proteinuria results from altered glomerular filtration barrier function.
Hypoalbuminemia contributes to edema.
Hyperlipidemia commonly accompanies nephrotic syndrome.
Thrombosis risk is increased in many nephrotic conditions.

title: Skin Graft and Flap Explained in Details

notes.text: Grafts and flaps
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Skin grafts are transferred without their own intact blood supply.
Flaps retain or reestablish a vascular supply as part of transfer.
Recipient bed vascularity is crucial for graft survival.
Reconstruction choice depends on tissue loss, exposed structures, and blood supply.

title: Hypertrophic Scar and Keloid Scar Explanation and Comparison

notes.text: Hypertrophic and keloid scars
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Hypertrophic scars remain within the boundaries of the original wound.
Keloids extend beyond the original injury margins.
Excess collagen deposition contributes to both conditions.
Recurrence is an important issue in keloid treatment.

title: Infectious Mononucleosis: Causes, Signs and Symptoms, Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Infectious mononucleosis
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Epstein-Barr virus is the classic cause of infectious mononucleosis.
Posterior cervical lymphadenopathy is a typical examination finding.
Atypical lymphocytes are largely reactive T cells in this setting.
Splenic enlargement raises concern about rupture with contact activity.

title: Portal Hypertension: Pathophysiology, Signs and Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Portal hypertension
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Increased portal pressure results from increased resistance, increased flow, or both.
Cirrhosis is a common cause of intrahepatic resistance.
Varices develop through portosystemic collateral pathways.
Ascites is a common complication of advanced portal hypertensive disease.

title: Decide Easily if You Hospitalize Your Pneumonia Patient or NOT? Using THIS

notes.text: Pneumonia severity assessment
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
CURB-65 incorporates confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and age.
Clinical judgment remains necessary because a score cannot capture every risk.
Oxygenation and ability to maintain oral intake influence disposition.
Comorbidity and social support are additional considerations.

title: Wound Healing by Primary and Secondary Intention

notes.text: Wound healing
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Primary intention describes healing of closely approximated wound edges.
Secondary intention involves filling a larger tissue defect with granulation tissue and contraction.
Fibroblasts produce extracellular matrix during repair.
Remodeling changes collagen organization and tensile strength over time.

Water balance disorders
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Diabetes insipidus causes impaired urinary concentration from deficient vasopressin action.
SIADH produces inappropriate water retention and hypotonic hyponatremia in the appropriate setting.
Serum osmolality helps interpret disorders of water balance.
Urine osmolality shows whether the kidney is appropriately diluting or concentrating urine.

title: Burkitt's Lymphoma: Types, Signs and Symptoms, Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Burkitt lymphoma
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
MYC dysregulation is central to Burkitt lymphoma.
Starry-sky pattern results from macrophages scattered among rapidly proliferating tumor cells.
High proliferation rate is a characteristic feature.
Tumor lysis syndrome is an important risk during treatment.
